history.dynasty: Korba zamindari family of Rajeshwar Dayal
history.summary: The Sarvamangala Temple stands on the banks of the Hasdeo river in Korba city and is dedicated to Goddess Sarvamangala, a form of Durga regarded as the guardian deity of Korba. According to the Korba district administration, the temple was built by the ancestors of Rajeshwar Dayal, a zamindar of Korba; it is surrounded by the Trilokinath Mandir, Kali Mandir and Jyoti Kalash Bhavan. Its most distinctive feature is an underground cave passage said to run beneath the Hasdeo river and emerge on the other side, which legend says Rani Dhanraj Kunwar Devi of the royal family used daily to reach the temple discreetly for worship. Coordinates are from a maps listing for the temple on Power House Road and are approximate.

name: Sarvamangala Temple
town_description: Korba is a major industrial city in Chhattisgarh, often called the power capital of the state, with large coal mines and thermal power plants (including NTPC and BALCO) around it. It lies on the banks of the Hasdeo river, which also shapes its religious geography, with riverbank shrines such as Sarvamangala and the Kanki temple nearby. The city is well connected by rail and road; the nearest airport is Swami Vivekananda Airport in Raipur.
